required_fixes: Minor (non-load-bearing): in the 'Behaviour of p-adic valuations' paragraph, the inference 'we cannot perform infinitely many such moves; consequently the process must reach a state with at most one positive p-valuation' is a non-sequitur on its own (finiteness of one move type does not force that state, since Confucius may avoid the pair). It is only valid because global termination was already proved in Part 1; this dependence should be stated, or the paragraph deleted since the determination argument does not use it.
Optional cleanup: Lemma 1 (product non-increase) is never used; it can be removed or kept as a remark.
verified_claims: Per-prime effect of a move: (v_p(m), v_p(n)) -> (min(a,b), |a-b|), via min/max valuations of gcd and lcm and lcm/gcd having valuation |a-b|.
Change in S = sum of Omega: Delta S = sum_p (max(a,b) - (a+b)) = -Omega(gcd(m,n)).

Lexicographic measure (K, S) strictly decreases in every case: g=1 gives K -> K-1 with Delta S = 0 (since L = mn > 1); g>1, m=n gives K -> K-1; g>1, m!=n gives L>1, K unchanged, Delta S <= -1. Lex order on N^2 is well-founded, so termination follows.
Terminal state: K <= 1 by definition of being stuck; K >= 1 is an invariant because each move outputs either g>1 or, when g=1, L=mn>1; hence exactly one integer M>1 remains.

Multiset gcd of p-adic valuations is invariant: gcd(a,b) = gcd(min(a,b), |a-b|) (including edge cases a=b, a=0, a=b=0), and replacing two elements preserves the gcd of the whole 2026-element multiset.
Terminal multiset {v_p(M), 0, ..., 0} has gcd v_p(M), so v_p(M) = g_p = gcd_i v_p(a_i) for every prime p, uniquely determining M = prod_p p^{g_p} independently of move choices.

Independent numerical checks: {4,8}->2 (matches Remark 1, and gcd(4,8)=4 differs, confirming the exponent-gcd vs min distinction); {6,10}->30; {6,10,15}->30; {12,18}->6; {2,3,6}->6 via two different move orders; {12,18,30}->30 via two different move orders; {4,8,16}->2; {2,2,2}->2.
Board size stays at 2026 throughout (each move replaces two entries by two), so the terminal gcd computation with 2025 zeros is correct.
summary: Correct and complete proof. Termination is established by a sound lexicographic descent on (number of nonunits, total Omega), with a clean case split on gcd=1 vs gcd>1 and m=n vs m!=n; the final state has exactly one nonunit because every move outputs at least one nonunit. Uniqueness follows from the per-prime invariant g_p = gcd of all p-adic valuations on the board (preserved since (a,b)->(min,|a-b|) is a Euclidean-algorithm step), which at termination forces v_p(M)=g_p. Hence M = prod_p p^{gcd_i v_p(a_i)}, verified on multiple small examples with varying move orders. The only blemish is a redundant intermediate paragraph whose 'consequently' is a non-sequitur without Part 1; it is not load-bearing. Lemma 1 is unused. No fatal gaps.
transfer_assessment: Reusable: prime-by-prime linearization of multiplicative operations — a move on (m,n) becomes independent coordinate moves (a,b)->(min(a,b),|a-b|) on exponent vectors, turning a number-theoretic process into a Euclidean-algorithm dynamic.
Reusable: lexicographic termination measure (count of distinguished objects, additive complexity) handles cases where one component is unchanged but the other strictly drops.

Reusable: multiset gcd as an invariant under Euclidean-type replacements; terminal-state evaluation (one nonzero entry plus zeros) then reads off the answer — a general 'invariant + normal form' uniqueness scheme that avoids analyzing strategy dependence directly.
Reusable observation: the answer is the exponent-wise gcd of the inputs, not their gcd; Remark 1's {4,8}->2 counterexample correctly flags the common wrong guess.

Potentially misleading if copied: the local argument 'sum of p-valuations decreases when both are positive, so eventually at most one is positive' is invalid without an independent global termination result; it must not be used as a standalone convergence proof.
Note: nothing depends on 2026; the argument works for any N >= 2 initial integers (and trivially N=1).
